subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: give one reason why recycling paper helps nature.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek kaaran batao ki kaagaz recycle karna prakriti ke liye achha kyon hai.
answer: Fewer trees are cut, water and energy are saved, and there is less garbage.

subject: evs
prompt_en: What natural material is each of these made from: glass, plastic, a steel plate?
prompt_hi: Ye kis natural cheez se bante hain: kaanch, plastic, steel ki plate?
answer: Glass: sand. Plastic: crude oil (petroleum). Steel: iron ore.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Bury a strip of jute (from an old sack) and a strip of plastic bag in a pot of moist soil. Predict what you will find after two months.
prompt_hi: Ek gamle ki geeli mitti mein purani bori ka jute ka tukda aur plastic ki thaili ka tukda daba do. Guess karo, do mahine baad kya milega?
answer: The jute will be softening and starting to rot and fall apart; the plastic will look nearly the same.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Spill a little water on a table. Put a cotton handkerchief on one drop and a piece of plastic sheet on another. Predict which one will soak up the water.
prompt_hi: Mez pe thoda paani gira do. Ek boond pe cotton ka rumaal rakho aur doosri pe plastic ki sheet. Guess karo kaun paani sokh lega.
answer: The cotton handkerchief soaks it up; plastic does not absorb water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Crude oil is natural. Why do we still call plastic human-made?
prompt_hi: Crude oil toh natural hai. Phir bhi plastic ko insaan ka banaya hua kyon kehte hain?
answer: Because people change the oil completely in factories to make plastic; plastic is not found anywhere in nature.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a jute bag and a plastic bag: one good point and one problem of each.
prompt_hi: Jute ke thaile aur plastic ki thaili ki tulna karo: dono ki ek achhi baat aur ek pareshaani.
answer: Jute: strong, reusable and rots away naturally, but heavier and can get mouldy if left wet. Plastic: light and waterproof, but doesn't rot, pollutes soil and water and harms animals.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Is silk natural or human-made? What about nylon?
prompt_hi: Resham (silk) natural hai ya insaan ka banaya hua? Aur nylon?
answer: Silk is natural (from silkworm cocoons); nylon is human-made (made from oil in factories).

subject: evs
prompt_en: Cows on Indian streets sometimes eat plastic bags along with food scraps. Using what you know about plastic, explain why that is dangerous and what people can do.
prompt_hi: Sadkon pe gaayein kabhi-kabhi khaane ke saath plastic ki thaili bhi kha jaati hain. Plastic ke baare mein jo jaante ho, usse samjhao ki ye khatarnaak kyon hai aur log kya kar sakte hain.
answer: Plastic doesn't break down, so it stays in the cow's stomach and can make it very sick; people should not throw food in plastic bags, should use cloth or jute bags, and should put waste in bins.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw arrows (or tell me) from each natural source to what is made from it. Sources: sand, iron ore, crude oil, cotton plant. Products: glass, steel, plastic, cloth.
prompt_hi: Har natural cheez se uski bani cheez tak teer banao (ya batao). Cheezein: ret, lohe ka ayask, crude oil, kapaas ka paudha. Bani cheezein: kaanch, steel, plastic, kapda.
answer: sand → glass; iron ore → steel; crude oil → plastic; cotton plant → cloth.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Glass comes from sand and plastic comes from oil, and sand and oil are natural, so glass and plastic are natural too!' Fix Golu.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Kaanch ret se aur plastic tel se banta hai, aur ret aur tel natural hain, toh kaanch aur plastic bhi natural hain!' Golu ko theek karo.
answer: They start from natural materials, but people change them a lot in factories (melting sand at very high heat, processing oil), so glass and plastic are human-made.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu how to tell whether a material is natural or human-made, with two examples of each.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki kaise pata karein koi material natural hai ya insaan ka banaya hua, dono ke do-do example dekar.
answer: Natural materials come from plants, animals or the earth and are used almost as they are (wood, cotton, wool, stone); human-made ones are made by people changing natural materials a lot (plastic, glass, steel, nylon).

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: name two natural materials and two human-made materials in your kitchen.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: apne kitchen ki do natural aur do insaan ki banayi cheezein batao.
answer: e.g. Natural: a wooden belan, a clay pot, a stone sil-batta, a cotton cloth. Human-made: steel utensils, plastic boxes, a glass jar.

subject: evs
prompt_en: What clothes would people wear in Ladakh in winter, and in Rajasthan in summer?
prompt_hi: Ladakh mein sardiyon mein log kaise kapde pehente honge, aur Rajasthan mein garmiyon mein?
answer: Ladakh: thick woollen clothes in layers, with caps and long woollen robes. Rajasthan: loose, light cotton clothes, with a turban (safa) or dupatta to shade the head from the sun.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In the Thar desert it is very hot in the afternoon. Predict: will it also be hot at midnight?
prompt_hi: Thar registaan mein dopahar mein bahut garmi hoti hai. Guess karo: kya aadhi raat ko bhi utni hi garmi hogi?
answer: No: desert nights can get quite cold, because the dry sand and clear skies let the heat escape quickly after sunset.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A family moves from coastal Kerala to Ladakh. Predict two things they will have to change in their daily life.
prompt_hi: Ek family Kerala ke samandar kinare se Ladakh shift hoti hai. Guess karo, unhe rozmarra ki zindagi mein kaunsi do cheezein badalni padengi.
answer: Any two: wear heavy woollens instead of light cotton; eat more of what grows or keeps well there (barley, thukpa, butter tea) and less fresh coconut and sea fish; keep the house warm in winter; use water carefully because it is a dry place.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why is Ladakh called a desert even though it is cold and has snowy mountains?
prompt_hi: Ladakh thanda hai aur wahan barfeele pahaad hain, phir bhi use registaan kyon kehte hain?
answer: Because it gets very little rain and is very dry; a desert means a place with very little rain, not a hot place.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare the Thar desert and Ladakh: one way they are alike and one way they are different.
prompt_hi: Thar registaan aur Ladakh ki tulna karo: ek baat jisme dono ek jaise hain, aur ek jisme alag.
answer: Alike: both get very little rain and have few plants. Different: the Thar is hot with sand dunes; Ladakh is cold, high and rocky with mountains.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Fishing is a common job on the coast. What common jobs might people do in the plains, and in the mountains?
prompt_hi: Samandar kinare machhli pakadna ek aam kaam hai. Maidaanon mein aur pahaadon mein log kaun se aam kaam karte honge?
answer: Plains: farming (wheat, rice, sugarcane) and dairy. Mountains: herding sheep, goats or yaks, growing apples or barley, and guiding tourists.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Antarctica is covered in ice, but scientists call it the world's biggest desert. Use what you learnt to explain why.
prompt_hi: Antarctica barf se dhaka hai, phir bhi scientist use duniya ka sabse bada registaan kehte hain. Jo seekha uske hisaab se samjhao kyon.
answer: It gets very little snow or rain each year, so it is extremely dry; a desert is defined by very little rain or snowfall, not by heat or sand.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Read this clue card: 'Very little rain, freezing winters, snowy mountains, people wear thick wool, eat barley and drink butter tea.' Which region is this? Point to it on the map and tell me which clues gave it away.
prompt_hi: Ye clue card padho: 'Baarish bahut kam, kadaake ki sardi, barfeele pahaad, log mote oon ke kapde pehente hain, jau khaate hain aur butter wali chai peete hain.' Ye kaunsa ilaaka hai? Map pe dikhao aur batao kin clues se pata chala.
answer: Ladakh, a cold desert in the far north of India; the clues are very little rain plus freezing cold, mountains and thick wool.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'All deserts are hot and full of sand dunes and camels.' Find the mistakes.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Saare registaan garam hote hain aur ret ke teelon aur oonton se bhare hote hain.' Galtiyan pakdo.
answer: Deserts are places with very little rain; some are cold, like Ladakh, and not all are sandy: some are rocky or icy.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu why people in the mountains and people on the coast eat and dress differently.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki pahaadon ke log aur samandar kinare ke log alag tarah ka khaana kyon khaate hain aur alag kapde kyon pehente hain.
answer: The weather and what grows are different: mountains are cold, so people wear wool and eat warming food and crops that grow there (barley, apples); coasts are warm and humid, so people wear light cotton and eat rice, fish and coconut.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: what is the one thing every desert has in common?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: har registaan mein kaunsi ek baat common hoti hai?
answer: Very little rain.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Which roof suits each place: heavy rain in Kerala, very little rain in Rajasthan? Sloping or flat?
prompt_hi: Kis jagah ke liye kaunsi chhat theek hai: Kerala mein bahut baarish, Rajasthan mein bahut kam baarish? Dhalaan wali ya sapaat?
answer: Kerala: sloping roof. Rajasthan: flat roof.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Pour a little water slowly onto a flat plate, and onto a plate tilted up on a book. Predict where the water will stay and where it will run off.
prompt_hi: Ek seedhi plate pe aur ek kitaab ke sahare tedhi rakhi plate pe dheere se thoda paani daalo. Guess karo, kahan paani rukega aur kahan beh jayega?
answer: It runs off the tilted plate and stays on the flat one, just as a sloping roof lets rain run off.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Two small huts in the Thar desert: one with thick mud walls, one with thin tin sheets for its roof and walls. Predict which is cooler inside at 3 pm.
prompt_hi: Thar registaan mein do chhoti jhopdiyan: ek moti mitti ki deewaron wali, ek patli 3 (tin) ki chhat aur deewaron wali. Guess karo, dopahar 3 baje andar se kaun zyada thandi hogi?
answer: The thick mud hut: thick mud lets heat in only slowly, while thin tin gets very hot very quickly.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do many houses in Rajasthan have flat roofs that people use in the evenings?
prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke kai gharon ki chhat sapaat kyon hoti hai, aur log shaam ko uska use kyon karte hain?
answer: It rains very little, so water doesn't collect much on a flat roof; the roof is used to sleep on cool nights and to dry clothes, grain or chillies, and some houses even collect the little rain that falls.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a traditional Kerala house and a traditional Ladakh house. What do their roofs look like, and why?
prompt_hi: Kerala ke paaramparik ghar aur Ladakh ke paaramparik ghar ki tulna karo. Unki chhat kaisi hoti hai, aur kyon?
answer: Kerala: steep sloping roofs, because monsoon rain is very heavy. Ladakh: flat roofs, because very little rain or snow falls there; the roofs are used to dry apricots and store fodder.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Lots of bamboo grows in the hills of Assam and Meghalaya. Why would people there build houses with bamboo?
prompt_hi: Assam aur Meghalaya ki pahaadiyon mein bahut baans ugta hai. Wahan log baans se ghar kyon banaate honge?
answer: Bamboo is found nearby, and it is strong, light and easy to work with, which is good for building raised houses.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Imagine building a house on a very hot, sunny, dry street. Name two features you would add to keep it cool, using what you learnt.
prompt_hi: Socho tum ek bahut garam, dhoop wali, sookhi jagah pe ghar bana rahe ho. Jo seekha uske hisaab se, ghar thanda rakhne ke liye do cheezein batao.
answer: Any two: thick walls, small or shaded windows, light-coloured walls and roof, trees around the house, a verandah or deep shade, a high ceiling.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Here is a description: 'A house on tall bamboo posts, with bamboo walls, a sloping thatch roof and a ladder to the door.' Draw it (or describe your drawing) and say what kind of place it suits.
prompt_hi: Ye varnan suno: 'Lambe baans ke khambhon pe ghar, baans ki deewarein, phoos ki dhalaan wali chhat, aur darwaze tak seedhi.' Iski drawing banao (ya batao kya banaoge) aur batao ye kis tarah ki jagah ke liye theek hai.
answer: A stilt house; it suits a place with heavy rain and floods, like parts of Assam.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Mud and bamboo houses are old-fashioned. Everyone everywhere should live in the same concrete flats.' What is Golu missing?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mitti aur baans ke ghar purane zamaane ke hain. Har jagah sabko ek jaise concrete flat mein rehna chahiye.' Golu kya bhool raha hai?
answer: Houses suit their land and weather: stilts for floods, thick mud walls for heat, sloping roofs for rain and snow; local materials are close at hand and suit the place, so one design doesn't fit everywhere.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu why houses in Assam, Rajasthan and the snowy hills look different.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki Assam, Rajasthan aur barfeele pahaadon ke ghar alag-alag kyon dikhte hain.
answer: Each suits its weather: Assam's floods and heavy rain call for stilts and sloping roofs; Rajasthan's heat and little rain call for thick mud walls and flat roofs; snowy hills need sloping roofs so snow slides off.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: why do houses in places with heavy rain or snow have sloping roofs?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jahan bahut baarish ya barf hoti hai, wahan ke gharon ki chhat dhalaan wali kyon hoti hai?
answer: So the rain and snow slide off.

subject: evs
prompt_en: When is your shadow longest: morning, noon or evening? And when is it shortest?
prompt_hi: Tumhari parchhai sabse lambi kab hoti hai: subah, dopahar ya shaam? Aur sabse chhoti kab?
answer: Longest in the early morning and late evening; shortest around noon.

subject: evs
prompt_en: At 8 in the morning the Sun is in the east. Predict: which direction will a stick's shadow point?
prompt_hi: Subah 8 baje Sooraj poorab (east) mein hota hai. Guess karo: dande ki parchhai kis disha mein padegi?
answer: West, on the opposite side from the Sun.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Fix a stick upright in the ground in a sunny spot. Mark the tip of its shadow at 9 am, 12 noon and 3 pm (look at the shadow, never at the Sun). Predict: which mark will be closest to the stick?
prompt_hi: Dhoop wali jagah pe ek danda seedha gaad do. Subah 9 baje, dopahar 12 baje aur 3 baje parchhai ke sire pe nishaan lagao (parchhai dekho, Sooraj ko kabhi seedha mat dekhna). Guess karo: kaunsa nishaan dande ke sabse paas hoga?
answer: The 12 noon mark: the shadow is shortest around noon, when the Sun is high.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Hold a red ball in sunlight. Predict: what colour will its shadow be?
prompt_hi: Dhoop mein ek laal ball pakdo. Guess karo: uski parchhai kis rang ki hogi?
answer: Dark grey, not red: a shadow is just where the light is blocked.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Shine a torch on a toy so its shadow falls on a wall. Predict: if you move the torch closer to the toy, what happens to the shadow?
prompt_hi: Torch se ek khilone pe roshni daalo taaki deewar pe uski parchhai bane. Guess karo: torch ko khilone ke aur paas le jaoge toh parchhai ka kya hoga?
answer: The shadow gets bigger, because the toy blocks more of the torch's light.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why is a shadow always on the opposite side from the light?
prompt_hi: Parchhai hamesha roshni ki ulti taraf hi kyon banti hai?
answer: Light travels in straight lines; the object blocks it, so the area behind the object, away from the light, stays dark.
